subject: Technical deep-dive recap: latency & throughput SLOs for FinTech Prod
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Carlos Mendez <carlos@fintech.io>, Samantha Reyes <samantha@fintech.io>
Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-03-20T09:15:00-07:00
Subject: Post-call: technical deep-dive recap & next steps

Hi Carlos / Sam —

Thanks again for the deep-dive this morning. Quick recap from Redwood and next steps so we stay aligned: 

Key pain points you called out:
- Inconsistent tail latency during peak business hours (observed p95 spikes to ~1.2s for single-shot prompts).
- Throughput requirements: sustained 350 QPS for inference pipelines running batched requests, with occasional bursts to 700 QPS during end-of-day reconciliation windows.
- Data residency: production inference must run in your us-west VPC for PII-sensitive flows.

Goals and success criteria you shared:
- P95 latency target <= 250ms for 2k token model paths (primary user flows).
- P99 latency target <= 500ms for same flows, or documented graceful degradation plan.
- Sustained throughput of 350 QPS with autoscaling headroom to 700 QPS.
- Deterministic tail behavior/99th percentile SLAs for business-critical endpoints.

Model / workload constraints we discussed:
- You expect to run a 13B encoder-decoder model for structured extraction and a separate 7B decoder-only summarization model for UX.
- Typical sequence lengths: 1k tokens (extract), 2k tokens (summaries).
- KV-cache reuse is high for the extract pipeline (prefix-heavy).

Topology and deployment notes:
- You prefer Private (VPC) deployment in us-west with a dedicated GPU pool per environment (staging/prod).
- Proposal: 8x A100-equivalent GPUs for extract (to meet 350 QPS steady) + burst pool of 4 additional GPUs for end-of-day spikes, with batching & KV caching enabled.
- Fallback plan: route to hosted lightweight quantized 4-bit model variants for non-critical traffic if local pool is saturated.

Action items (owners):
1) Redwood: share SLO engineering worksheet + rough cost estimate (Marissa) — ETA today EOD.
2) FinTech: provide 3 sample request traces and typical traffic curve by hour (Carlos) — ETA Tue 3/23.
3) Redwood infra: quick feasibility note on VPC onboarding + KMS integration (Vivek, Dylan) — ETA Mon 3/22.

Attachments: FT-SLO-requirements.pdf (draft SLO worksheet)

If I missed anything or a goal is misstated, flag it here and I’ll update. Otherwise I’ll loop in our solutions engineer (Dylan) to start sizing.

Thanks —
Marissa

Thanks Marissa — this looks right. A couple clarifications from our side:

- The 350 QPS figure is for the extract pipeline only; the summarization path is lighter (~60 QPS) but has tighter latency expectations because it powers our customer-facing UI.
- Sequence lengths: extract avg 800 tokens, 95th ~1.6k; summarize avg 1.2k, 95th ~2.1k.
- For residency: we can provide a VPC peering diagram and the list of subnets — I’ll attach the network diagram to the traces request.

We’ll bundle the sample traces + hourly traffic curve and send by Tue as requested. One ask for Redwood: can you confirm whether your KV-cache approach supports cross-request caching for identical prefixes across users? That will strongly affect our batching strategy.

—Carlos

Carlos — quick answers and a couple of asks from infra: 

- KV-cache: yes, Redwood supports prefix/KV reuse across requests when the prefix text is identical and policies allow. Cache keys are per-model and can be scoped by tenant or global within a VPC deployment. We typically enable cross-request reuse in Private deployments unless customers want stricter isolation.
- Batching strategy: we recommend adaptive continuous batching with a 15ms latency budget for the batching window on UI-critical flows; for extract (batch-heavy) we suggest 60ms window to maximize GPU efficiency while meeting p95 targets.
- Preliminary sizing (very rough): for the extract 13B model: ~8 A100-eq GPUs for steady 350 QPS (with 60ms batching). For summary 7B model: 2 GPUs should be sufficient for 60 QPS with 15ms batching. Burst pool: 4 GPUs.

Questions we need from you to firm up numbers:
1) Confirmation on tenant isolation: do you need strict per-tenant model cache separation?
2) Typical request payload sizes (KB) for both pipelines.
3) Are there synchronous UI timeouts we need to respect (hard deadlines)?

I’ll attach a quick topology sketch for the suggested VPC deployment (redwood-deployment-topology.png) and a short table mapping batch window -> expected p95/p99.

Thanks —
Dylan

Notes on SLOs (from worksheet):

- Autoscaling threshold: scale-up when 75% of dedicated pool steady utilization is reached; burst policy lifts from the burst pool with 30-60s warmup depending on model.
